column1: # 1. Aia Ka ʻAlakeka Ma Kaipāpaʻu? = Is There An Alligator At Kaipāpaʻu?

# 2. Eia ka moʻolelo e pili ana i ka ʻalakeka o Kaipāpaʻu, ʻo ia hoʻi ke ahupuaʻa ma waena o Hauʻula a me Lāʻiemaloʻo. = There is a story about an alligator in Kaipāpaʻu, the land division between Hauʻula and Lāiemaloʻo.
# 3. Ua ʻike ʻoe i ia mea? = Have you seen it?
# 4. He ʻalakeka kupaianaha ʻo ia. = It is a magical alligator.
# 5. Peʻe ʻo ia ma ke kai. = It hides itself in the ocean.
# 6. ʻIke ʻoe i nā puʻu o kona kua? = Do you see the bumps of his back?
# 7. ʻIke ʻoe i ka miomio o kona ihu? = Do you see his pointy nose?
# 8. ʻIke ʻoe i kona kua laulā ā nui? = Do you see his large broad back?
# 9. ʻIke ʻoe i kona huelo lōʻihi? = Do you see his long tai?
# 10. He aha lā ia mea? = What is he?
# 11. ʻAʻole nō ia he ʻalakeka maoli nona ka niho wakawaka. = He’s not a real alligator with sharp teeth.
# 12. He pōhaku loloa nō ia. Ua kohu ʻalakeka ia mea nei. = He’s a long rock that looks like an alligator.
# 13. ʻO Loko Kai ʻO ʻAlakeka kēia. = This is Alligator Pond.
# 14. He wahi leʻaleʻa nohoʻi kēia i nā keiki o ke kaiāulu. = It is a fun place for children of the neighborhood.
# 15. Hele lākou i ʻaneʻi e ʻolu ai ke kino i ka wela o ka lā. = They come here to escape the heat of the day.
# 16. Piʻi nā keiki i nā puʻu o kona kua. = Children climb the bumps of his back.
# 17. ʻImi lākou i kēlā ʻano mea kēia ʻano mea e noho ana ma ka loko kai. = They search for different ocean creatures.
# 18. Hauʻoli nā keiki i ka pāʻani like i ke one ma ʻaneʻi. = Children love to play together in the sand.
# 19. ʻEli ka lima i ke one ā kūkulu ʻia nā mea like ʻole me ka pākeke one. = They dig with their hands and build things with their sand bucket.
# 20. Hele ā ʻolu ke kino o ke kamaliʻi i ke kai pāpaʻu o kēia loko kai. = Children cool off their bodies in the shallow of the sea pond.
# 21. Akā naʻe ... ʻo ka lēkei mai ka ihu iho ka mea leʻaleʻa nui nō. = But ... jumping from his nose into the water is the most fun thing to do.
# 22. Hauʻoli ka poʻe keiki. = The children are so happy.
# 23. He keu ā ka leʻaleʻa! = It is so much fun!
# 24. Akā naʻe, aia ā napoʻo ka lā, e hoʻi aku nō i ka hale. = When the day is done, we must return home.
# 25. Aloha ā hui hou aku i kekahi lā wela! = So, good-bye until the next hot day.
